title: Cooper Flagg Makes Time for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
htmlContent:
Cooper Flagg has spent most of his young life being the busiest person in any room. From Maine to Duke to the No. 1 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, free time has been scarce. But the Mavericks forward andreigning Kia NBA Rookie of the Year made one thing clear when he was asked whether he has jumped into the new Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: he is carving out time for it, even if it's not as much as he'd like.

"I've Played a Little Bit"

Asked if he had gotten his hands on the latest entry in the long-running shooter franchise, Flagg gave an honest answer that will sound familiar to anyone juggling a demanding job and a new video game release.

"I've played a little bit," Flagg shared with LandonBuford.com after the Mavericks beat the Utah Jazz 112-100 on Friday Night at the American Airlines Center in Dallas. "You know, we've been a little bit busy, a little busy with the season starting, but I'm trying to play a little bit."

He did not hesitate when it came to his favorite part of the game.

"You know, multiplayer is fun," he said. "I mean, I play COD pretty much every year. So you use it to relax and take my mind off all the stress."

That last line says a lot about how Flagg approaches life as one of the most scrutinized young athletes in sports. The controller isn't just entertainment. It's a release valve.

A Rookie Season That Raised the Bar

The stress Flagg mentions is understandable given the expectations he carries. As a rookie in 2025–26, he led all first-year players in scoring at 21.0 points per game while adding 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.2 steals across 70 games. He joined Michael Jordan as the only rookies since 1973–74 to lead their team in total points, rebounds, assists and steals.

Flagg also became the youngest player in NBA history to score 50 points in a game, dropping 51 on the Orlando Magic on April 3. He finished the year with four 40-point games, the most by a rookie since Allen Iverson in 1996–97. All of that came while Dallas went 26-56 in a rebuilding season.

The Rookie of the Year race was tight. Flagg received 56 first-place votes to 44 for his former Duke teammate, Charlotte's Kon Knueppel, becoming the third Maverick to win the award after Jason Kidd and Luka Doncic. Now in his second season, he is the face of a franchise, and every off-night is dissected.

Why Multiplayer Is the Perfect Escape

It makes sense that multiplayer is where Flagg spends his gaming time. Call of Duty's online modes offer quick matches, constant action and the kind of competition that appeals to someone wired the way he is. A few rounds can fit between film sessions, travel days and treatment, and they don't demand the long commitment of a story campaign.

Already on Call of Duty's Radar

When it was suggested that Flagg should team up with the Call of Duty franchise, the idea wasn't far-fetched. He has already worked with the series. Over the summer, Flagg took part in a Modern Warfare 4 grudge match against football star Jeremiyah Love at Fanatics Fest, giving fans an early look at the game and a glimpse of the Mavericks forward's competitive streak away from the hardwood.

It's easy to see why the partnership works for both sides. Call of Duty gets one of the most marketable young athletes in the world, someone whose fan base skews toward the same audience that buys the game every fall. Flagg gets to connect with fans in a relaxed setting and show off a personality that doesn't always come through in postgame interviews.

Balancing the Court and the Controller

For now, basketball remains Flagg's clear priority. His own words—"a little busy with the season starting"—reflect the reality of an NBA schedule that leaves little room for marathon gaming sessions. The Mavericks are counting on him to take another leap in year two, and he has spoken about wanting to sharpen his ball handling, playmaking and outside shooting.

Still, there's value in the balance he describes. Staying sharp over an 82-game season isn't only about physical recovery. Mental rest matters too, and if a few multiplayer matches help Flagg shut his mind off after a tough loss or a long flight, Mavericks fans should have no complaints.

The reigning Rookie of the Year may only be playing Modern Warfare 4 "a little bit" right now. But between his summer appearance with the franchise and his annual habit of picking up the newest game, Cooper Flagg's connection to Call of Duty looks like it's here to stay.
excerpt: Dallas Mavericks forward and reigning Kia NBA Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg says he's been carving out time to play Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 despite a busy season, leaning on multiplayer matches to decompress from the pressures of life as the NBA's most scrutinized young star.
